title: Universal property of localization at an arbitrary multiplicative subset
statement: Let $A$ and $C$ be commutative rings, $U\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset, and $U^{-1}A$ the ring of fractions $a/u$ ($a\in A$, $u\in U$), where $a/u=a'/u'$ exactly when some $v\in U$ annihilates $au'-a'u$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. If $f:A\to C$ is a ring homomorphism for which $f(u)$ is a unit of $C$ for every $u\in U$, then there is a unique ring homomorphism $g:U^{-1}A\to C$ with $g(a/1)=f(a)$ for every $a\in A$. It is given by $g(a/u)=f(a)f(u)^{-1}$. Consequently two ring homomorphisms from $U^{-1}A$ that agree after precomposition with $A\to U^{-1}A$ are equal.
